name: The Samaritan leper who returned
charge: One of ten: turning back to glorify God with a loud voice, and giving thanks at his feet
summary: Ten lepers stood afar off and cried for mercy, and were sent to shew themselves to the priests as the law commands. As they went they were cleansed. Nine kept going. One, a Samaritan, turned back, fell on his face at his feet and gave thanks. He alone was told, thy faith hath made thee whole.
offense: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. The other nine had obeyed the letter, going to the priests; this one came back to the one who had sent them.
judgment: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole. Ten were cleansed of leprosy; one went home whole.

entries.commentary: This is the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing. The leper stays outside the camp; the priest goes forth out of the camp to him and looks whether the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper. The priest does not heal the plague; he examines the man after the healing and carries out the cleansing the Most High commanded.

For him that is to be cleansed the priest commands two birds alive and clean, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop. One bird is killed in an earthen vessel over running water. The living bird, with the cedar wood, the scarlet, and the hyssop, is dipped in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water; the priest sprinkles him that is to be cleansed seven times, pronounces him clean, and lets the living bird loose into the open field.

He that is to be cleansed washes his clothes, shaves off all his hair, and washes himself in water, and comes into the camp; but he tarries abroad out of his tent seven days. On the seventh day he shaves all his hair off his head, his beard, and his eyebrows, washes his clothes and his flesh in water, and is clean.

On the eighth day he brings two he lambs without blemish, one ewe lamb of the first year without blemish, three tenth deals of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering, and one log of oil. The priest that makes him clean presents him with these things before the Most High at the door of the tabernacle. One he lamb is offered for a trespass offering with the log of oil, waved for a wave offering, and slain in the holy place: as the sin offering is the priest's, so is the trespass offering; it is most holy.

The priest takes of the blood of the trespass offering and puts it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot. Of the log of oil the priest pours into his own left hand, sprinkles of it with his finger seven times before the Lord, and puts oil upon the ear, the thumb, and the toe, upon the blood of the trespass offering; the remnant of the oil he pours upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to make an atonement for him before the Lord.

The priest then offers the sin offering to make an atonement for him that is to be cleansed from his uncleanness, kills the burnt offering, and offers the burnt offering and the meat offering upon the altar; the priest makes an atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

If he be poor and cannot get so much, the law makes provision: one lamb for a trespass offering to be waved, one tenth deal of fine flour mingled with oil, a log of oil, and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, such as he is able to get, the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. The same order is kept for the poor man: the blood of the trespass offering upon the right ear, the right thumb, and the right great toe, the oil sprinkled seven times and put upon the same places, and the rest of the oil upon his head. This is the law of him in whom is the plague of leprosy, whose hand is not able to get that which pertaineth to his cleansing.

The Most High tells Moses and Aaron that when Israel comes into the land of Canaan, and he puts the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of their possession, the owner shall come and tell the priest, saying, It seemeth to me there is as it were a plague in the house. The priest commands that the house be emptied before he goes in, that all that is in it be not made unclean; then he looks on the plague, and if it be in the walls with hollow strakes, greenish or reddish, in sight lower than the wall, he shuts up the house seven days. If at the seventh day the plague be spread in the walls, the stones in which the plague is are taken away and cast into an unclean place without the city; the house is scraped within round about, the dust poured out without the city into an unclean place, and other stones and other mortar are put in their place.

If the plague come again and break out in the house after the stones were taken away and the house scraped and plastered, the priest looks, and if the plague be spread, it is a fretting leprosy in the house: it is unclean. He breaks down the house, the stones of it, the timber, and all the mortar, and carries them forth out of the city into an unclean place. He that goes into the house while it is shut up is unclean until the even, and he that lies or eats in the house washes his clothes.

If the priest comes in and looks, and the plague hath not spread in the house after it was plastered, the priest pronounces the house clean, because the plague is healed. The house is cleansed the same way as the leper: two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop; one bird killed in an earthen vessel over running water, the house sprinkled seven times, and the living bird let go out of the city into the open fields; so he makes an atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.

The chapter closes the summary: this is the law for all manner of plague of leprosy and scall, for the leprosy of a garment and of a house, for a rising, a scab, and a bright spot, to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law of leprosy.

David charges his own soul and all that is within him to bless the holy name of the Most High and to forget not His benefits. Those benefits are named: He forgives all iniquities, heals diseases, redeems life from destruction, crowns with lovingkindness and tender mercies, and renews the youth like the eagle's. The Most High executes righteousness and judgment for all that are oppressed. Hear that clearly: it does not say for all people, it says for all that are oppressed.

He made known His ways unto Moses, His acts unto the children of Israel. Look at that: His acts unto the children of Israel, not to every nation. When Israel fled Egypt there were oppressed nations who came out with us; the Bible calls them strangers. But the ways of the Most High were made known to Moses and Israel. -

The Most High is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, plenteous in mercy. He has not dealt with us after our sins nor rewarded us according to our iniquities. This is heavy because Christ came to forgive Israel of their sins. That mercy and grace is to Israel, and it is not so that we could continue in sin. As far as the east is from the west, so far He removes our transgressions; He pities them that fear Him, for He knows we are dust. -

Man's days are as grass and as a flower of the field; the wind passes over it and it is gone. But the mercy of the Most High is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear Him, and His righteousness unto children's children. This is why we must teach our children in every generation, so they receive that same mercy. The covenant is to such as keep His commandments and remember them to do them. To do them is an action word. -

The Most High has prepared His throne in the heavens and His kingdom rules over all. The angels that excel in strength bless Him by doing His commandments and hearkening to the voice of His word. All His hosts and works in every place of His dominion bless Him; and David returns to charge his own soul: bless the Lord.

verses.text: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off:
And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.
And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,
And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.
And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
This shall be the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought unto the priest:
And the priest shall go forth out of the camp; and the priest shall look, and, behold, if the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper;
Then shall the priest command to take for him that is to be cleansed two birds alive and clean, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop:
Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.
Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases;
